newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurds say Turkey bombs civilians.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds say Turkey bombs civilians.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish group on Wednesday accused Turkey of entering northern Iraq and carrying out artillery and air strikes against Iraqi Kurdish settlements in the hunt for Kurdish separatist guerrillas.
The Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) said in a statement that Turkish soldiers had crossed the border in a three-pronged drive on Sunday. It did not give the size of the Turkish force.
The KDP said Turkish air force planes bombed three villages and artillery fire struck five other settlements on Monday.
Turkish foreign ministry spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.
"As a result of the repeated shelling, bombardment and harassment, inhabitants of the area...fled their homes," the statement said.
Turkey frequently strikes across the mountainous border against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas who use bases there in their fight for self rule in southeastern Turkey.
Turkey hosted U.S.-sponsored peace talks last week at which the KDP and a rival Iraqi Kurdish militia agreed to extend a ceasefire after two months of fighting.
But the KDP later said it was not bound by part of the joint declaration after the talks that suggested the Iraqi Kurds had agreed to help Turkey oust the PKK from the region.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in 12 years of fighting between Turkish troops and the PKK.
